issues.what: OCR rationale says "The ASR transcript E11 states Musk's announcement and Cybertruck deployment", but the ASR observation the student saw is just the backend/limitations metadata. The transcript text is only opened at turn 10 (request_0011).
issues.why_bad_to_teach: It teaches the student to describe a record's content before reading it, which is hallucination.
issues.ideal: Justify OCR from the frames alone (visible on-screen text such as FOX LOCAL / KNN.NEWS / LOST HILLS SHERIFF'S EVENT), and say the transcript is still to be read.

issues.what: Rationale for READ_RECORD E20 says it will verify "whether the Automotive News article actually supports the claim", but E20 is the Dirt Legal blog (R4). Automotive News is E19, which was just read.
issues.why_bad_to_teach: It teaches mixing up which source sits behind which evidence id.
issues.ideal: "E19 returned only Automotive News navigation text (Volvo items), so read E20 (Dirt Legal) as another account of the Cybertruck redirection."

issues.what: "Reading E22 to gather additional source confirmation before finalizing the fact-check report." This is boilerplate. E22 is a fourth secondary write-up of the same Musk tweet, after E19-E21. The turn 6/8/9 rationales also share one template ("Reading Exx (...) to verify the claim ...").
issues.why_bad_to_teach: It teaches generic "gather more" justifications and reading near-duplicate secondary pages.
issues.ideal: Either skip E22, or say what it adds (e.g. it quotes Musk's apology tweet directly). Use the reading budget on a targeted search for any actual withdrawal report instead.

issues.what: The get_frames rationale says the frames are needed "to check on-screen text and spoken content from the ASR transcript E11". Frames cannot show spoken content, and OCR had already pulled the on-screen text.
issues.why_bad_to_teach: The stated purpose of the action does not match what the action can deliver.
issues.ideal: "Get one clear frame per shot from E13 (0.6/3.79/17.36/34.68 s) to see what each shot shows (studio vs field footage of the trucks)."

issues.what: The only search was one combined query. All hits were about the diversion, and no follow-up query targeted the claimed event itself (e.g. "Musk pulls Cybertrucks LA fires" / fact-check). The report and answer then leave "Whether Musk ordered any withdrawal at another time remains unverified."
issues.why_bad_to_teach: It teaches leaving the claim's central assertion open without one targeted search for it.
issues.ideal: Run one more text search aimed at a withdrawal or recall report (or a fact-check of the title). Then state either that none was found or what was found.

issues.what: Limitation "4 of 8 candidate pages failed to load and were not examined; an earlier or other copy may exist among them." This is provenance-task boilerplate. In this claim check the failed pages (police1, americanfaith, justthenews, cybertruckownersclub) are about the deployment, not copies of the video.
issues.why_bad_to_teach: It teaches pasting provenance limitations into a different task type.
issues.ideal: "4 of 8 result pages failed to load; their snippets also describe the delivery diversion and Starlink use, so they were not examined in full."

issues.what: T1 copies the overall task verbatim ("Fact-check the following claim, which circulated as the title ..."). The rationale is generic: "one workspace does it".
issues.why_bad_to_teach: It teaches the planner not to decompose (what does the video say, is there any report of a withdrawal, when was the clip aired).
issues.ideal: Keep one workspace, but give its Scope explicit points: transcribe and describe the segment; search for reports of the deployment and of any withdrawal; compare the two.

issues.what: The verifier flagged "unsupported_assertion/critical", yet the REVISED ANSWER is word-for-word the original. The likely culprit is "including powering Starlink terminals in areas without connectivity.[E21][E22]". In the visible text, Starlink appears in E20 and the R2/R7 snippets, not in E21/E22.
issues.why_bad_to_teach: The exported answer may carry an assertion that its cited ids do not support, and the 'revision' fixed nothing.
issues.ideal: Cite E20 for the Starlink role (or drop the clause), or have the revise step change the flagged sentence.

good_patterns: Video-first sequence: ASR, OCR, video_structure, frames per shot, then external search. The full transcript (C9v) is read before the report is written.
Noticed that E19 returned only unrelated Automotive News navigation text (Volvo items) and moved on instead of citing it.

The report separates what the narration says from what the frames show ("These images show parked vehicles, not a withdrawal operation"). Frame timestamps (0.594/3.795/17.358/34.683 s) are copied correctly.

The final verdict is scoped ("misleading as a title for this video"), and the limitations name what is still unverified: a later withdrawal, how long the deployment lasted, and the primary announcement.
cannot_judge: The E11 transcript content is truncated (+1641 chars), so the quoted narration ("They're already in use by first responders", Malibu Starlink/free Wi-Fi, owners collecting Starlink equipment) could not be checked against the ASR text.
E21/E22 page text is truncated, so I could not confirm whether they mention Starlink, i.e. whether the verifier's critical flag is about that clause or a different sentence.
The frame images were not visible, so the descriptions of E15-E18 (two presenters, trucks beside trailers) could not be checked.
summary: A sound, well-ordered claim check: the video is transcribed and sampled, mainstream reports of the diversion are read, and the verdict that the title misrepresents a deployment as a withdrawal is reasonably scoped. The one major issue is the OCR rationale, which describes the ASR transcript's content before it was ever read. Minor issues: a source mix-up in a rationale, boilerplate or templated read rationales on near-duplicate pages, a verbatim GIA task, no targeted search for the claimed withdrawal, a provenance-style limitation pasted into a fact-check, and a final answer left unchanged despite a critical unsupported-assertion flag.
